title: chore: Preview PRs with mermaid-live-editor on Netlify
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

We will now deploy a live editor preview for develop, next, master branches and all PRs.
This should make reviews easier for the maintainers.

Implements https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/3348

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

We can try adding live editor as a git submodule. 
But I would rather not make any changes to the mermaid repo right now, apart from adding one file. 

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/community/development.md#3-update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [x] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
By the way, if you add a `set -euxo pipefail` to the front of your bash script, it will automatically exit the bash script if any command fails (so we don't need any `|| exit` bits)!

- `set -e`: Exits the bash script if any command fails.
- `set -x`: print out each line before running it (helping for debugging GitHub Actions, although I wouldn't do this in an users facing scripts)
- `set -u`: Exit the script trying to use unset variables, e.g. `$NON_EXISTANT_VARIABLE`.
- `set -o pipefail`: if any command in a pipe fails, make the whole pipe return an error code.

```suggestion
set -euxo pipefail

# We have to use npm instead of yarn because it causes trouble in netlify

# Link local mermaid to npm
pushd packages/mermaid
npm link
popd

# Clone the Mermaid Live Editor repository
git clone https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-live-editor.git

# Change to the repository directory
cd mermaid-live-editor
```
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests adding `set -euxo pipefail` to ensure the script exits if any command fails, addressing the issue of unchecked command return codes in the bash script.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding 'set -euxo pipefail' to the bash script and provides a concrete code suggestion to refactor the script.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Should we rename this file `.bash` if it's explicitly a bash script?

It's just so we don't run this under another POSIX shell, like `dash` (default `/bin/sh` shell on Ubuntu).
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests renaming the file extension to `.bash` to explicitly indicate it's a bash script and avoid being run under a different POSIX shell, which is a language/environment-specific convention.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body: As far as I know, the first line would make it execute in bash no matter what the file extension is.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> As far as I know, the first line would make it execute in bash no matter what the file extension is.

Not necessarily.

If you do try to execute the file directly (e.g. with `./scripts/editor.sh`), then it will run in `bash` using the shebang. But if you do `sh ./scripts/editor.sh` (or `. ./scripts/editor.sh` from a non-bash shell) , then it will still run in `sh` (and if you do `node ./scripts/editor.sh`, it will try to run in `node`, and fail!).

I've had to do a lot of POSIX shell scripting on platforms like OpenWRT and Alpine Linux, where `bash` isn't available (and even on Ubuntu, `dash` is preferred over `bash` for performance reasons), so it's good to know what's a POSIX shell script and what's a bash script from the filename.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests renaming the file from .sh to .bash to ensure it runs under bash rather than another POSIX shell.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
Very likely it is not necessary at all, but exit have 0 as default status. If any other script on top of that is relying on that, it can be misleading, because it masks its behavior:
```
./editor.sh && echo "success"
```
If it is exactly what is needed let it be as it is.

Just in case, `$?` returns exit code of previous command
comments.label_reasoning: The comment points out that using `exit 0` masks the actual exit behavior of the script, potentially misleading callers who rely on the exit code to determine success or failure — a mismatch between intended and actual behavior.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: The `|| exit`s were auto-added by my shellcheck extension. I've removed them based on @aloisklink's suggestion.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential issue with the default exit 0 masking script behavior, implying the exit code handling may need to be reconsidered.
